states.activities:
No data will flow into or out of NHS England. This Agreement permits continued retention and processing of data already disseminated only.

The data disseminated under this Agreement will be linked to Screening data for breast cancer, this data was previously provided by Public Health England under ODR1516_167.

All data retained is strictly confidential and will be stored on a secure database at QMUL. Access to the database will be controlled using a user-specified username and password. No other users other than the Senior Data Manager will have access to identifiable data. There will be no attempt or requirement to re-identify individuals from the pseudonymised data being processed.

The data will only be processed by substantive employees of QMUL who have received appropriate training in data protection and confidentiality.

states.objective:
Queen Mary, University London (QMUL) requests to retain the National Disease Registration Service (NDRS) data previously disseminated by Public Health England (PHE) under the reference ODR1516_167. Following the dissolution of PHE in October 2021 the NDRS function transferred to NHS Digital, since this time NHS Digital have merged into NHS England, which is now responsible for assessing requests for access to/continued access to NDRS data.

QMUl received the data to investigate the benefit of the National Breast Screening Programme in terms of the effect on breast cancer mortality and its detrimental impact on overdiagnosis. This work is still ongoing and outputs are still in the process of being produced.

The DSA permits the retention and processing of identifiable NDRS Cancer Registry data previously disseminated by PHE. The data disseminated covers all individuals who have a cancer registration of invasive or in situ breast cancer between 01/01/2016 to 31/12/2017, and died or were diagnosed between the ages of 47-89. The data disseminated also contains information for control groups.

QMUL is the sole data controller and data processor and is responsible for ensuring that data is only processed in line with the purposes set out in this Agreement.

states.activities:
No data will flow to NHS England for the purposes of this Data Sharing Agreement (DSA).

The data disseminated under this Agreement will be linked to Screening data for breast cancer, this data was previously provided by Public Health England under ODR1516_167.

The Data will be stored on servers at QMUL.

The Data will not leave: England/Wales at any time.

Access is restricted to employees or agents of QMUL who have authorisation from the Principal Investigator.

All personnel accessing the Data have been appropriately trained in data protection and confidentiality.

The identifying details will be stored in a separate database to the linked dataset used for analysis. All analyses will use the pseudonymised dataset. There will be no requirement and no attempt to reidentify individuals when using the pseudonymised dataset.

Analysts from QMUL will analyse the Data for the purposes described above.

datasets.name: NDRS Cancer Registrations

states.expected_benefits:
The study aims to feed into a body of research that may be used by relevant bodies to improve the national screening programme for breast cancer.

The team have two planned outputs outstanding, the estimation of the effect of the NHS Breast Screening Programme on stage of disease, and the estimation of its effect on case fatality, in particular estimating the proportions of the survival benefit attributable to stage of disease and the proportion attributable to variations in therapy by screening status.
states.expected_output:
Progress results will be posted on the study web pages and in peer-reviewed medical journals, after submission to and approval by the appropriate stakeholder.

The outputs will not contain NHS England Data and will only contain aggregated information with small numbers suppressed as appropriate in line with the relevant disclosure rules for the dataset(s) from which the information was derived.

The team have published two of the planned outputs from this project, the effect of the NHS breast screening on mortality from breast cancer (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33223536/) and the effect of the programme on incidence of breast cancer (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35851849/). It is taking longer than expected to finish the other two planned outputs, the estimation of the programme's effect on incidence of advanced stage disease and its effect on case fatality.
states.objective:
Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) requires access to NHS England data for the purpose of the following research project:

An on-going case-control study to evaluate the NHS Breast Screening Programme (NHSBSP) (ODR1516_167)

The following is a summary of the aims of the research project provided by QMUL:

QMUL received the data to investigate the benefit of the National Breast Screening Programme in terms of the effect on breast cancer mortality and its detrimental impact on overdiagnosis. This work is still ongoing and outputs are still in the process of being produced.

The DSA permits the retention and processing of identifiable NDRS Cancer Registry data previously disseminated by PHE. The data disseminated covers all individuals who have a cancer registration of invasive or in situ breast cancer between 01/01/2016 to 31/12/2017, and died or were diagnosed between the ages of 47-89. The data disseminated also contains information for control groups.

The following NDRS datasets are already held: 

- NDRS Cancer Registrations

The level of the Data is: 

- Identifiable

QMUL is the research sponsor and the controller as the organisation responsible for ensuring that the Data will only be processed for the purpose described above.

The lawful basis for processing personal data under the UK GDPR is:

Article 6(1)(e) - processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller;

The lawful basis for processing special category data under the UK GDPR is:

Article 9(2)(j) - processing is necessary for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with Article 89(1) based on Union or Member State law which shall be proportionate to the aim pursued, respect the essence of the right to data protection and provide for suitable and specific measures to safeguard the fundamental rights and the interests of the data subject.
states.title: An on-going case-control study to evaluate the NHS Breast Screening Programme (NHSBSP) (ODR1516_167)
states.yielded_benefits:
The team have published two of the planned outputs from this project, 
(1) the effect of the NHS  breast screening on mortality from breast cancer (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33223536/), showing a substantial and significant reduction in breast cancer mortality with screening, and a longer lasting protection in older women.
(2) The effect of the programme on incidence of breast cancer (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35851849/), finding that overdiagnosis is at worst modest, and that there is no increase in aggressive therapy with screening.

 It is taking longer than expected to finish the other two planned outputs, the estimation of the programme's effect on incidence of advanced stage disease and its effect on case fatality. However, these are at an advanced stage, and we anticipate that work will be complete by late 2024.
